start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the published clips for my site." It calls tool:read-published-clips with your pursuit database and the site's use, and gets back each published clip with short links to its file and its still.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it reads the clip rows of your pursuit database through a fenced select, and shares each clip's files from your own Files session by name, under /published-clips/.
instructions: 1. Publish a clip with the publish step: it keeps the file at /published-clips/<id>.<ext>, the cover at <id>.jpg, and for a comparison the two stills at <id>-left.jpg and <id>-right.jpg, and sets recording_moment.published_file_name.
2. Ask for the clips: the site sends use {purpose, surface} from its own list (publish and site for the public site; members and members-page for the members programs).

3. Read the answer: each clip has cut_url (the file, or the combined render for a comparison), picture_url (its cover, for a single clip or reel) and, for a comparison, pair.left and pair.right each with picture_url (their still).
4. Links last 900 seconds. Ask again for fresh links; never store them.

worked_examples.title: Read the site's clips
worked_examples.ask: Read the published clips for my site
worked_examples.given: A published clip in the database whose person holds a live grant for the use.
worked_examples.hands_back: { clips: [ { id, moment, kind, aspect, captured_day, cut_url, picture_url, pair? } ] }, each URL short-lived; a clip whose grant is withdrawn is not in the answer.
